messages:
Alex: Quick brain-dump: I prototyped a 'consensus resume' alternative to full KV restores. Idea: keep a tiny authoritative ledger per-stream (hash checkpoints + op-count) and let edge nodes attempt a fast resume by comparing checkpoints. If mismatch, fall back to stricter recon.
Mira: Ledger sounds heavier than a token. How is it different from the ResumeToken idea?
Alex: Token is a single snapshot. Ledger is an append-only, tiny sequence of checkpoints (every K tokens) plus op-counts so we can detect drift windows rather than exact equality. Helps with non-deterministic model behaviors.
Devon: I like drift windows. Practical question: where is the ledger stored? durable store vs inline with tokens?
Alex: Durable small-index store (S3-like) with per-tenant retention. Edge caches recent ledger entries. Ledger entries are <checkpoint_hash, op_count, model_epoch>.
Raj: Ok, but what's the handshake? edge asks upstream: give me latest checkpoint >= my token.op_count. Upstream returns best-match checkpoint id and a delta length to replay.
Sylvie: Metrics we need: resume_path (consensus|token|reconstruct), replay_len, mismatch_detected, fallback_reason. Also tag by model and route.
Tasha: Risk: if ledger retention is short, edges may not find a match and we trigger heavy reconstructs under load. Need admission backpressure.
Alex: Agreed. Proposed policies: keep last 10 checkpoints (~one per 100 tokens), but have a soft TTL. If no match and request is high-priority (SLA tier), try proactive reconstruct from dedicated replica. Otherwise return 409-ish to client (fast-fail) with resume_suggest header.
Mira: 409 to client seems rough for UX. Can we stream a partial fast-response while kicking off strict reconstruct in background and patch if needed?
Devon: Patching is acceptable for some chat use-cases but not for side-effectful requests (webhooks, payment ops). We need a per-route side_effects flag to disallow background patching.
Raj: Security: ledger entries are small but still sensitive. ACLs + signed fetch URLs. Also HMAC the checkpoint metadata to prevent forged retokens.
Sylvie: Billing: replay work costs tokens and CPU. Chargeable metrics should reflect resumed replay tokens and background reconstruct time, and be visible per-tenant.
Tasha: Edge memory/cpu: when a resume starts, reserve a replay budget per-stream. If budget exhausted, degrade to 'consensus-skip' mode where we accept potential divergence but mark the response as "best_effort":true.
Alex: We'll expose resume_mode in route config: {policy: 'fast-consensus'|'token-only'|'strict' , allowed_patch: bool, replay_budget_ms: int}. Defaults: hosted -> fast-consensus with allowed_patch=true; dedicated/enterprise -> strict by default.
Mira: Need heuristics to auto-upgrade policy: if divergence_rate > 0.05% over 24h or if webhook routes show retries in logs.
Devon: Implementation notes: 1) compact checkpoint format (blake2b-64, op_count, model_sig), 2) small read path in edge with short-circuit, 3) background warming RPC with low-priority queue.
Raj: KMS note: sign checkpoint+ledger entries with route key. infra-bot, create ticket for HSM/KMS design.
infra-bot: Created INF-4780: "Checkpoint ledger signing + ACLs" (https://tracker/internal/INF-4780).
Sylvie: Observability ticket too: INF-4781 for resume_path/replay_len/divergence signals.
Alex: Action items: Alex -> draft ledger proto and handshake flow; Mira -> prototype UX for background-patch behavior; Devon -> edge resource budget design and graceful-degrade states; Raj -> KMS signing plan; Sylvie -> telemetry dashboards mockups.
Tasha: Sync next Tue? I'll bring SRE distro for stress tests.
Alex: Yes. Quick note: avoid client-side long-lived tokens unless HMAC+short TTL. Server-side ledger references are preferred.
Mira: Thanks everyone. Small ask: can we avoid the word "resume" in client-visible errors? Use "session_reconnect" to avoid confusing product folks.
Alex: Good call. End of thread.
